project_capsule.brief: Create a software to turn my Markdown notes into a searchable static site with tags and backlinks.
project_capsule.problem_statement: Markdown notes are currently not easily discoverable and navigable; the user needs an automated way to publish notes as a static website with full-text search, tag-based browsing, and backlink navigation between notes.
goals: Ingest a collection of Markdown notes and generate a static website (HTML/CSS/JS) from them.
Preserve Markdown formatting and structure in the generated site.
Provide full-text search across generated content in the static site.
Support tags so users can browse/filter notes by tag.
Detect and render internal links between notes and generate backlinks ("linked from") sections.
Produce a build output that can be hosted on common static hosting without requiring a server-side runtime.
non_goals: Building a dynamic, server-rendered web application or requiring a database/server at runtime.
Real-time collaborative editing or multi-user permissions/roles.
A full Markdown editor; the source of truth remains existing Markdown files.
Version control or change tracking beyond what exists in source files.
Automatic note-taking, summarization, or AI-based content generation.
Guaranteeing compatibility with every Markdown extension; only a defined subset will be supported.

constraints.text: Output must be static HTML/CSS/JS that can be hosted on any web server
Must process standard Markdown syntax as input

assumptions.text: Notes exist as a set of Markdown (.md) files stored as individual files that can be read from a local directory and/or repository.
Internal links between notes can be identified via a consistent convention (e.g., Markdown links to filenames/paths or wiki-style links like [[Note Title]]).
Tags can be derived from a consistent convention (e.g., YAML front matter tags and/or inline #tags) and do not require manual curation in the generated site.
Search will be implemented client-side (e.g., a prebuilt index shipped with the site) to keep the output fully static.
A command-line build workflow is acceptable (run a build command to generate the site).
The site will be used by a single user or small group without access control needs.

open_questions.text: What Markdown/linking conventions must be supported for internal links and backlinks (standard Markdown links, relative paths, wiki-links [[...]], Obsidian-style links, etc.)?
How should tags be specified and parsed (YAML front matter, inline hashtags, a dedicated syntax), and what are the rules for tag normalization (case, spaces, nesting)?
What scale is required (approx. number of notes and total size), to choose an indexing/search approach and performance targets?
What is the desired information architecture: required pages and navigation (home, all notes, tags index, per-tag pages, per-note page layout)?
What hosting/deployment target is expected (local file browsing, GitHub Pages, Netlify, other), and are there constraints on relative paths/base URLs?
What Markdown flavor/features must be supported (e.g., CommonMark/GFM; tables, footnotes, math/LaTeX, mermaid/diagrams, code highlighting), and is there an existing renderer preference?
Should the build be incremental (only rebuild changed notes) and/or provide a watch mode for local preview?
Should the site expose outgoing links, backlinks only, or a full graph view; and how should broken links be handled (warn, fail build, render as plain text)?
Are there specific design or theming requirements for the generated site?
Should the tool run as a CLI, GUI application, or build script integration?

success_metrics: Given an input directory of Markdown notes, the tool generates a static site output directory successfully (build completes without errors on a supported environment).
All Markdown files in the input set are rendered into accessible HTML pages in the output (excluding explicitly configured ignores).
Full-text search returns relevant results for queries that match note titles and body text, with search interaction remaining responsive at the confirmed target note scale.
For any valid internal link between notes, the destination note page includes a backlinks section listing the source note after a successful build, and backlinks are rendered as clickable links.
Tag index pages are generated such that selecting a tag shows all notes containing that tag, and each note page displays its associated tags.
Generated site loads and functions in modern browsers without errors.
stakeholders: Readers/consumers of the published notes (if shared)

glossary.definition: A website consisting of pre-generated files (e.g., HTML/CSS/JS) served without server-side rendering or a runtime database.
A lightweight markup language using plain text formatting syntax that converts to HTML.
A label associated with a note, used to group and browse notes by topic.
A reverse reference showing which other notes link to the current note.
Search that matches terms in the content of notes (not only titles/metadata), typically via a prebuilt index for static sites.

plan_package.executive_summary: This candidate delivers a monolithic CLI tool (O1) that turns a directory of Markdown notes into a fully static HTML/CSS/JS site with tags, backlinks, and client-side full-text search. Delivery follows a thin-slice plan: first produce a working build pipeline that renders notes to HTML and passes ingestion/build correctness tests, then incrementally add tags, link/backlink graphing, search, and final deployment/polish features. Key risks around link/tag conventions (K2/K3) are managed by making those conventions explicit configuration before implementing their dependent features, and by adding build-time reporting/warnings rather than failing builds by default.

requirements.text: The system MUST accept a user-specified local directory path as input and recursively discover Markdown files, including all files with the ".md" extension by default.
requirements.rationale: Core ingestion capability is required to process a collection of Markdown notes stored as files in a directory tree.

requirements.text: The system MUST generate a static build output consisting only of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and other static assets that can be hosted/served without any server-side runtime or database dependency.
requirements.rationale: A primary constraint is that the result is a purely static site deployable on common static hosting.

requirements.text: The system MUST parse each discovered Markdown file using at least CommonMark-compliant syntax and generate a corresponding HTML page for every input Markdown file not explicitly excluded by configuration.
requirements.rationale: All notes must be rendered into accessible HTML pages; CommonMark compliance ensures support for standard Markdown syntax.

requirements.text: The system MUST preserve standard Markdown formatting and structure in generated HTML (including headings, lists, emphasis, links, images, and code blocks).
requirements.rationale: The site must faithfully render notes so that the published content matches the source structure and formatting.

requirements.text: The system MUST provide a command-line interface (CLI) build workflow that accepts at minimum an input directory path and an output directory path and executes the full build pipeline to generate the site output directory.
requirements.rationale: A CLI is the minimum interface needed to run builds and produce a static output directory from notes.

requirements.text: The build process MUST either complete successfully for a valid input set or report clear, actionable error messages on failure.
requirements.rationale: Build reliability and actionable failures are required for usability and for meeting the build success metric.

requirements.text: The generated site MUST include client-side full-text search across note titles and body content that executes entirely in the browser without requiring server-side processing or server requests to perform searches.
requirements.rationale: Search is a core feature and must work on static hosting with no backend runtime.

requirements.text: The build process MUST generate a full-text search index artifact at build time and include/ship it with the static site output for use by the client-side search feature.
requirements.rationale: A prebuilt index is required to enable fast client-side search while keeping the output fully static.

requirements.text: The system MUST detect internal links between notes and, at minimum, correctly resolve standard Markdown relative links to other Markdown notes in the input set into navigable links to the corresponding generated HTML pages.
requirements.rationale: Internal navigation between notes is a core feature; at least standard Markdown relative links must work end-to-end.

requirements.text: For each note that is linked to by other notes, the generated note page MUST include a backlinks section listing all notes that link to it, and each backlink entry MUST link to the source note page.
requirements.rationale: Backlinks provide required reverse navigation (“linked from”) and are a stated success criterion.

requirements.text: The system MUST extract tags from each note using at least one supported tagging convention that is user-selectable/configurable (e.g., YAML front matter tags field and/or inline "#tag" syntax) and associate the extracted tags with the note in the generated site.
requirements.rationale: Tag extraction is required to enable tag-based browsing across different note/tagging conventions.

requirements.text: Each generated note page MUST display its associated tags and render each tag as a navigable link to the corresponding tag page.
requirements.rationale: Displaying tags as links completes the tag-browsing loop and supports discoverability.

requirements.text: The generated site MUST include a tags index page and per-tag pages that list all notes associated with each tag.
requirements.rationale: Users need tag-based browsing to discover and navigate notes by topic.

requirements.text: The generated site MUST load and function correctly in the current stable releases of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge without JavaScript errors that block core functionality (navigation, search, backlinks, tags).
requirements.rationale: The site must work reliably for readers in modern browsers.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD provide configurable rules for internal link parsing and support additional link syntaxes beyond standard Markdown relative links (e.g., wiki-style links like "[[Note Title]]"), as selected by the user.
requirements.rationale: Different note collections use different internal-link conventions; configurability improves compatibility and reduces adoption risk.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD provide configurable tag normalization rules (e.g., lowercasing and trimming whitespace) applied consistently across tag pages and note tag displays.
requirements.rationale: Normalization prevents duplicate tags and ensures predictable tag browsing behavior.

requirements.text: The generated site SHOULD include a home/landing page and a navigation structure that provides access to an all-notes listing, the tags index, and the search feature, and these navigation entry points SHOULD be reachable from any note page.
requirements.rationale: A minimal information architecture and global navigation are needed for discoverability and navigability.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD emit build-time warnings for unresolved internal links (including source file and link text), SHOULD not fail the build by default for such links, and SHOULD render unresolved links in a clearly non-navigable manner in the output.
requirements.rationale: Broken-link handling improves authoring feedback without preventing builds for minor issues.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD allow configuration of a base URL and/or path prefix so the generated site can be deployed under a subdirectory (e.g., GitHub Pages project sites).
requirements.rationale: Static hosting deployments commonly require non-root base paths; configurability prevents broken asset and link URLs.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD allow users to exclude specific files or directories from the build via a configuration file or CLI option.
requirements.rationale: Users often need to skip drafts/templates; exclusion support aligns with the requirement to omit explicitly ignored files.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD support GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) extensions including tables, strikethrough, task lists, and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting.
requirements.rationale: GFM support improves fidelity for common Markdown note collections and preserves expected formatting features.

requirements.text: For collections of up to 1,000 notes on a modern consumer device, full-text search results SHOULD be returned and rendered in under 500 ms.
requirements.rationale: A concrete performance target helps ensure search remains responsive for a reasonable default scale.

requirements.text: The system COULD support incremental builds that only regenerate pages for notes that have changed since the last build.
requirements.rationale: Incremental builds improve build times and authoring workflow for larger note collections.

requirements.text: The system COULD provide a local development server and live-reload/watch mode that automatically rebuilds and refreshes the browser when source files change.
requirements.rationale: A watch mode and live preview improve usability during active note authoring.

requirements.text: The generated site COULD include an interactive graph visualization showing link relationships between notes.
requirements.rationale: A graph view can enhance discoverability beyond backlinks, but is not required for the core use case.

requirements.text: The system COULD support user-selectable themes and/or custom CSS injection for visual customization of the generated site.
requirements.rationale: Theming improves personalization without changing core content generation functionality.

requirements.text: The generated site COULD render outgoing links from each note as a dedicated section alongside the backlinks section.
requirements.rationale: Showing outgoing links can provide additional bidirectional context but is not required to satisfy the backlinks goal.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Prepare a test input directory with nested subdirectories containing Markdown files: root/a.md, root/sub/b.md, root/sub/deeper/c.md, and a non-Markdown file root/sub/d.txt. Run the CLI build with the input directory path and a valid output directory path.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Build completes successfully and the build log (or output manifest) shows discovery of exactly the three .md files (a.md, b.md, c.md) and does not include d.txt.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Run a build on a fixture directory. Inspect the output directory contents recursively and list file types/extensions. Serve the output with a simple static file server and open the site in a browser.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: All emitted files are static assets (e.g., .html, .css, .js, images, fonts, .json for search index). No server-side runtime or database dependency is required to view pages; the site loads and renders pages when served statically.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Prepare a fixture with N Markdown files (N>=3) and a configuration that excludes one specific Markdown file. Run the build. Count generated HTML note pages and verify a one-to-one mapping for non-excluded files.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: For each non-excluded input Markdown file, exactly one corresponding HTML page exists in output; excluded Markdown files do not have generated HTML pages.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Create a fixture Markdown file containing headings (H1/H2), ordered and unordered lists, bold/italic emphasis, links, images, and fenced code blocks. Build the site and open the generated HTML for that note. Inspect the HTML DOM or rendered page for each element type.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria:
Rendered HTML preserves the structure and formatting for all specified elements: headings map to appropriate

/

, lists to
    /
      , emphasis to /, links to , images to , and code blocks to 
       with content intact.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Invoke the CLI with required arguments: input directory path and output directory path. Record exit code and presence of output directory contents.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: CLI accepts the input and output paths, completes a full build pipeline, exits with code 0, and creates the output directory with generated site files.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Case A: Run build with a valid fixture input. Case B: Run build with an invalid input directory path (non-existent) or a malformed configuration file. Capture exit codes and stderr/stdout messages.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Case A: build completes successfully with exit code 0. Case B: build exits with non-zero code and emits a clear, actionable error message indicating the cause (e.g., missing directory or invalid configuration) and how to fix it.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Build the site for a fixture dataset with known terms in note titles and bodies. Open the site in a browser with network disabled or using a static file server that blocks outbound requests. Use the search UI to query a term that exists in a note body and another that exists only in a title.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Search returns correct results for both queries entirely in-browser without any server requests, and results link to the corresponding note pages.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Run a build and inspect the output directory for the search index artifact(s) (e.g., search-index.json or equivalent). Open the site and verify the search UI loads the index file from the output directory (via local static server).
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: A search index artifact is generated at build time and present in the output directory, and the client-side search loads it from the static output to perform queries.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Prepare two notes: note-a.md containing a standard Markdown relative link to note-b.md. Build the site and open the rendered page for note-a. Click the link to note-b.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: The link in note-a navigates to the generated HTML page for note-b without errors, and the URL corresponds to the output path for note-b.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Prepare three notes: note-a links to note-c; note-b links to note-c; note-c has no outgoing links. Build the site and open note-c page. Inspect backlinks section and click each backlink.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Note-c page includes a backlinks section listing note-a and note-b, and each backlink is a clickable link that navigates to the corresponding source note page.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Configure one supported tag convention (e.g., YAML front matter tags or inline #tag) per configuration. Create notes with tags following that convention. Build the site and inspect the generated metadata for each note (as rendered on page).
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Tags are extracted according to the selected convention and associated with the correct notes in the generated site (each note shows the expected tag set).

acceptance_tests.procedure: Using a fixture with at least two tags, build the site and open a note page. Inspect the tags section and click each tag link.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: Each tag is displayed on the note page and each tag is a navigable link that routes to the corresponding tag page.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Build the site with notes containing tags. Locate the tags index page and at least one per-tag page. Verify listed notes for each tag.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: A tags index page exists and lists available tags. For each tag, a per-tag page exists that lists all and only the notes containing that tag.

acceptance_tests.procedure: Build the site and open it in the latest stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Navigate between notes, run a search query, and open a tag page. Monitor the browser console for errors.
acceptance_tests.pass_criteria: All core functionality (navigation between notes, search, backlinks display, tag browsing) works in each browser without JavaScript errors that block functionality.

options.summary: Custom-built monolithic CLI pipeline (single-process) that scans Markdown files, extracts metadata/tags/links, builds a note graph with backlinks, renders HTML via templates, generates a client-side search index, and writes a fully static HTML/CSS/JS output (implementation can be Node.js- or Python-based).

components.name: CLI Orchestrator
responsibilities: Parse CLI args (source dir, output dir, config/theme options)
Validate configuration and inputs
Run pipeline stages in order and report build summary/errors

components.name: Source Scanner & Front Matter Parser
responsibilities: Recursively discover Markdown files
Read file contents and parse front matter (title, tags, metadata)
Normalize identifiers (slugs) from file paths/titles for cross-referencing

components.name: Content Analyzer (Links/Tags) & Graph Builder
responsibilities: Parse note bodies for internal links (Markdown links and optional wiki-links)
Resolve links to note identifiers/slugs
Build forward links and compute backlinks (reverse edges)
Extract and normalize tags (front matter and/or inline tags)
Produce a unified in-memory NoteGraph used by rendering and search

components.name: Markdown Renderer
responsibilities: Convert Markdown to HTML via a configurable renderer pipeline
Support code block syntax highlighting (as configured)
Provide hooks to inject tag lists and backlinks into per-note HTML

components.name: Template & Theme Renderer
responsibilities: Render per-note pages using templates/layouts
Generate site-level pages (home, all-notes, tag index, per-tag pages)
Apply theme/layout configuration (including user overrides if supported)

components.name: Search Index Builder
responsibilities: Build a client-side full-text search index from note titles/body text
Serialize the index (and any supporting documents) to static JSON/assets

components.name: Output Emitter & Asset Copier
responsibilities: Write generated HTML pages and search assets to the output directory
Copy static assets (CSS/JS/images/fonts) into the output directory
Optionally emit auxiliary files (e.g., sitemap/manifest) if configured

components.name: Client-Side Runtime (Search UI)
responsibilities: Load the prebuilt search index in the browser
Provide a search UI with interactive results
Link results to generated note pages

interfaces.contract: Pass validated build configuration including sourceDir, outputDir, and parsing/rendering options.
Provide NoteFile[] with {slug/id, rawMarkdown, frontMatter, filePath} for analysis and graph construction.
Provide NoteGraph with per-note {rawMarkdown, title, tags, outLinks, backLinks} to drive rendering.
Provide RenderedNote[] with {slug, title, htmlContent, tags, backLinks} for templating into full pages.
Provide NoteGraph (or equivalent note corpus data) required to build the client-side search index.
Provide PageOutput[] with {relativePath, htmlString} and referenced static assets to write to the output directory.
Provide serialized search index assets (e.g., search-index.json and supporting files) to be emitted to output.
Browser fetches search index asset(s) from the static output (e.g., GET /search-index.json); runtime JS is included in pages.

pros: Straightforward end-to-end build flow and debugging (single CLI program)
No server runtime required; outputs static HTML/CSS/JS
Easy to package as a single tool users run against a notes directory
Good performance for small-to-medium note sets with in-memory processing
cons: Harder to extend safely compared to a formal plugin architecture
Potential scalability limits (memory/time) on very large note sets without caching/incremental rebuilds
Implementation stack choice (Node vs Python) affects ecosystem fit, performance, and distribution approach

risks: Large collections can lead to high memory usage if all notes and derived structures are held in memory
Client-side search index size can grow large and impact browser load/interaction time
Tight coupling between graph-building and rendering may complicate future extensibility

options.summary: Plugin-based build core with defined lifecycle hooks (ingest/transform/render/emit) and a shared build context or data store; features like Markdown parsing, link/backlink resolution, tags, templates, and search are implemented as swappable plugins.

components.name: Core Build Engine / Orchestrator
responsibilities: Load configuration and discover/register plugins
Define and execute lifecycle hooks (ingest, transform, render, emit)
Manage plugin ordering and dependency constraints
Provide stable APIs for plugins to read/write shared build state

components.name: Shared Build Context / Central Data Store
responsibilities: Hold normalized note records, metadata, and derived indices
Expose APIs for plugins to query and mutate notes, tags, and link relationships
Act as the handoff mechanism across lifecycle stages

components.name: Ingestion Plugin
responsibilities: Scan source directory and load Markdown files
Create note entries in the shared build context

components.name: Metadata & Tag Extraction Plugin
responsibilities: Parse front matter and extract tags from configured conventions
Normalize tags and attach metadata to note entries

components.name: Link Resolution & Backlink Plugin
responsibilities: Detect internal links in note bodies (Markdown links and optional wiki-links)
Resolve targets to canonical note identifiers
Compute backlinks and store link graph structures in the shared context

components.name: Markdown Render Plugin
responsibilities: Convert Markdown to HTML with configurable renderer and extensions
Apply syntax highlighting or other content transforms
Store per-note rendered HTML in the shared context

components.name: Theme / Template Plugin
responsibilities: Render final pages from shared context data (notes, tags, backlinks)
Generate site-level pages (tag indexes, per-tag pages, listing pages)
Support user-supplied theme overrides (if implemented)

components.name: Search Index Plugin
responsibilities: Build a static client-side search index from notes in the shared context
Emit index asset(s) into the build outputs

components.name: Emit Plugin
responsibilities: Write generated pages and assets to the output directory
Handle base URL/relative path rewriting for deployment targets (if configured)

interfaces.contract: Invoke ingest hook; plugin populates shared context with discovered notes.
Invoke transform hook; plugin reads notes and writes normalized metadata/tags into shared context.
Invoke transform hook; plugin reads note bodies and writes link graph + backlinks into shared context.
Invoke render hook; plugin reads raw Markdown and writes rendered HTML into shared context.
Invoke render hook; plugin reads rendered notes + metadata and produces final PageOutput entries.
Invoke render hook; plugin reads note corpus and produces static search index asset(s).
Invoke emit hook; plugin writes pages and assets from shared context to the output directory.

pros: High extensibility via swappable plugins (Markdown flavors, search providers, themes, extra outputs)
Separation of concerns improves maintainability and isolated testing
Supports multiple user workflows and future features without rewriting the core
cons: Higher upfront complexity designing a stable plugin API and shared data model
Plugin ordering/dependencies complicate debugging and user configuration
Potential performance overhead and subtle bugs from shared mutable state

risks: Plugin API and data model may evolve, causing breaking changes and ecosystem churn
Third-party plugin compatibility/versioning can become an ongoing maintenance burden
Conflicting plugins can cause non-obvious behavior and hard-to-reproduce build failures

options.summary: Build on an existing static site generator (e.g., Eleventy/11ty) and add custom configuration/plugins for wiki-links/backlinks, tag pages, and a search index; relies on the SSG's built-in watch/dev server and templating ecosystem.

components.name: SSG Core (External Dependency)
responsibilities: Provide the main static site build engine, templating, and collections/pagination
Process Markdown input via configurable Markdown library
Offer watch mode and a dev server (where supported by the SSG)

components.name: SSG Configuration Module
responsibilities: Configure input/output directories and template formats
Register collections/filters/shortcodes used by templates
Configure Markdown parsing options and extensions

components.name: Backlinks / Link Graph Plugin
responsibilities: Scan note content for internal links (Markdown links and optional wiki-links)
Compute backlinks map and make it available to templates via the SSG data model

components.name: Tag Pages Generator
responsibilities: Generate tag index and per-tag listing pages using SSG pagination/collections
Expose tag counts and filtering logic to templates

components.name: Search Index Build Step
responsibilities: Build a static search index from rendered content or source notes
Write index assets to the output directory as part of (or after) the SSG build

components.name: Theme / Layout Templates
responsibilities: Define note page layout, tag pages, and global navigation
Include search UI elements and backlink sections in page layouts
Provide CSS styling and any shared template components

components.name: Client-Side Runtime (Search UI)
responsibilities: Load the search index and provide interactive search in the browser
Support navigation to notes from search results

interfaces.contract: Register configuration, collections, filters, and shortcodes into the SSG build lifecycle.
Integrate backlinks data into the SSG's data pipeline so templates can render per-note backlinks.
Define pagination/collection rules so the SSG generates tag index and per-tag pages.
Run as a build hook/transform to produce search index assets into the SSG output directory.
Provide merged content and data (notes, tags, backlinks) as template inputs to render final HTML.
Serve static output; client runtime JS loads search index assets from the output site.

pros: Leverages mature SSG functionality (templating, collections, watch/dev server, incremental rebuilds where available)
Reduces custom code by building atop a battle-tested toolchain and community plugins
Faster time-to-value for common site features (pagination, navigation, layouts)
cons: Tight coupling to the chosen SSG architecture and upgrade cadence
Backlinks/wiki-link parsing often requires custom logic beyond the SSG defaults
Distribution as a standalone tool is harder; users must adopt the SSG environment

risks: SSG major-version changes can break custom plugins/configuration
Wiki-link/backlink behavior may vary with Markdown plugins and require ongoing compatibility work
Search integration may be constrained by what the SSG build lifecycle exposes without deeper customization

options.summary: Multi-stage build pipeline with intermediate artifacts (e.g., JSON per note plus a global graph manifest) enabling caching and incremental rebuilds; each stage can be re-run independently and the final stage assembles the static site output.

components.name: Ingestion Stage
responsibilities: Read source Markdown files and collect raw content and file metadata
Write a standardized intermediate representation (one artifact per note) to a build/cache directory

components.name: Analysis Stage
responsibilities: Parse intermediate note artifacts to extract structured metadata (title, tags)
Detect internal links and enrich intermediate artifacts with extracted structure

components.name: Graph Build Stage
responsibilities: Aggregate enriched note artifacts to build a global site graph
Compute backlinks and tag relationships
Write a site-wide manifest (graph + tag indexes) for downstream consumption

components.name: Render Stage
responsibilities: Render note HTML and index pages using enriched artifacts and the global manifest
Generate client-side search index assets from note content/metadata
Write rendered outputs to a temporary build output directory

components.name: Site Assembler / Final Emitter
responsibilities: Assemble rendered files and static assets into the final output directory
Manage cache keys and incremental rebuild decisions (e.g., hash-based invalidation)

interfaces.contract: Intermediate per-note artifacts (e.g., JSON files) are written by ingestion and read/updated by analysis.
Enriched per-note artifacts are consumed to produce a global graph/tag manifest artifact.
Render stage consumes the global manifest plus per-note artifacts to produce HTML pages and search index assets.
Rendered files in a temporary build directory are assembled and emitted to the final output directory.

pros: Enables incremental builds by re-running only stages impacted by changed inputs
Improves scalability by avoiding the need to hold all derived structures in memory at once
Decoupled stages are easier to test, benchmark, and troubleshoot independently
cons: More complex build orchestration and cache management
Clean builds may be slower due to additional disk I/O for intermediate artifacts
Intermediate representation becomes a de facto internal API that must be versioned

risks: Cache invalidation and dependency tracking bugs can lead to stale or inconsistent site output
Intermediate artifact schema changes can break builds or require migrations
Increased pipeline complexity introduces more failure points (partial stage failures, corrupted cache)

chosen.rationale: Choose O1 (custom monolithic CLI pipeline) because it satisfies the static-output constraint and all MUST requirements with the least upfront framework/API design, enabling fast iteration and thin-slice delivery. The single-process in-memory graph is appropriate for the confirmed near-term target (up to ~1,000 notes per R22) and keeps debugging straightforward while link/tag conventions are still being clarified (Q1/Q2).
chosen.high_level_dataflow: CLI Orchestrator (C1) reads args/config -> Source Scanner & Front Matter Parser (C2) discovers .md files and parses per-file metadata -> Content Analyzer & Graph Builder (C3) extracts tags and internal links, resolves them to canonical note IDs, and computes backlinks -> Markdown Renderer (C4) converts Markdown to HTML (with sanitization policy) -> Template & Theme Renderer (C5) wraps rendered note content into per-note pages and generates site-level pages (home/all notes/tags) -> Search Index Builder (C6) builds a static index artifact -> Output Emitter (C7) writes HTML/assets/index into output -> Client-Side Runtime (C8) loads the index and provides in-browser search UI.

milestones.name: Thin slice: CLI skeleton + recursive Markdown ingestion + per-note HTML rendering

deliverables.text: CLI command that accepts input directory and output directory, validates arguments, and runs an end-to-end build (R5).
Recursive discovery of .md files by default with an internal file manifest/report for discovered vs ignored files (R1).
CommonMark-compliant Markdown parsing and HTML generation for each non-excluded Markdown file (R3, R4).
Static site output directory containing only static assets (HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/images/fonts as needed) suitable for static hosting (R2).
Build error handling baseline: clear actionable messages for invalid input/config and readable per-file parse/render failures (R6).

exit_criteria: Build produces one HTML page per non-excluded Markdown file and no server/runtime dependencies are required to view pages.
Build produces a deterministic file list for a given input set (stable ordering in manifests/log output).

milestones.name: Tags: extraction + normalization + tags index/per-tag pages + tag navigation

deliverables.text: Configurable tag extraction source(s) implemented for at least one convention (e.g., YAML front matter tags and/or inline #tags) (R11).
Tag normalization pipeline implemented (case/whitespace rules) and applied consistently across pages (R16).
Per-note tag display with each tag rendered as a navigable link (R12).
Tags index page plus per-tag pages listing associated notes (R13).
Tag extraction report (counts, normalization outcomes) to support debugging convention issues (mitigates K3).

exit_criteria: Tag pages are generated deterministically (stable tag ordering and stable note ordering per tag).

milestones.name: Links & graph: internal link resolution + backlinks section

deliverables.text: Canonical note identifier/slug strategy defined and implemented (path-based by default) to support stable cross-references and collision handling (mitigates K10).
Internal link resolver for standard Markdown relative links to other notes; emitted HTML links navigate to the correct generated pages (R9).
Backlink computation and per-note backlinks section that links back to source notes (R10).
Link-graph diagnostics output (e.g., counts + unresolved targets list) to support convention debugging (mitigates K2/K9/K12).

exit_criteria: Backlink generation handles cycles without crashing/hanging (basic graph consistency check).

milestones.name: Search: build-time index generation + client-side search UI

deliverables.text: Build-time search index artifact generated and shipped in output directory (R8).
Client-side search UI that loads the shipped index and supports searching titles and body text fully in-browser (R7).
Basic performance instrumentation/reporting for index size and query timing on fixture sets to inform R22 (mitigates K5).

exit_criteria: Search works with network disabled and returns results linking to note pages.

milestones.name: Polish & compatibility: broken-link warnings, base URL, GFM extensions, browser QA

deliverables.text: Broken-link handling: build-time warnings for unresolved internal links (with source context), do not fail build by default, and render unresolved links as clearly non-navigable (R18).
Base URL / path-prefix configuration applied consistently across generated links/assets to support subdirectory deployments (R19).
GFM extensions support plan implemented for the agreed subset (e.g., tables/strikethrough/task lists) and syntax highlighting behavior (R21).

exit_criteria: End-to-end acceptance run: AT1–AT14 pass in sequence.
Cross-browser check complete: site functions in stable Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge without JS errors blocking core functionality (R14).
Deployability spot-check: output works when hosted under a subdirectory base path.

risk_register.description: Incorrect or unsupported Markdown flavor parsing/rendering (e.g., CommonMark vs GFM extensions such as tables/footnotes/code fences) causes content loss, broken layouts, or misleading HTML output (relates to Q6).

mitigation.text: Explicitly select and document a supported Markdown flavor; add golden-file render tests for representative notes; provide a compatibility mode matrix and a build-time warning list for unsupported constructs.

risk_register.description: Ambiguous or unsupported internal link conventions (relative paths vs wiki-links) lead to broken links and incorrect/incomplete backlink graphs (relates to A2, Q1).

mitigation.text: Make link-convention support an explicit configuration; implement a deterministic resolver with precedence rules; fail or warn on unresolved links based on strictness setting; add fixture-based tests for Q1 scenarios.

risk_register.description: Tag extraction conventions and normalization are undefined/inconsistent (front matter vs inline #tags; case/spacing/duplicates), producing incomplete or confusing tag navigation (relates to A3, Q2).

mitigation.text: Define a single normalization pipeline (case-folding, trimming, delimiter rules); support configurable sources (front matter / inline) with explicit precedence; add a validation report listing tags and counts.

risk_register.description: At the user’s required scale, the build process becomes unacceptably slow, crashes, or hangs due to large numbers of notes or very large files, including memory spikes during parsing/indexing (relates to Q3).

mitigation.text: Stream processing where feasible; cap in-memory caches; provide progress logging; add stress tests at expected upper bounds and document hardware recommendations.

risk_register.description: Client-side full-text search index size/performance scales poorly (large index, slow load, high memory), causing unresponsive search and degraded UX at target scale (relates to A4, A4/Q3).

mitigation.text: Collect target scale requirements (Q3); choose an indexing approach appropriate to scale; implement chunking/lazy loading; add performance budgets (index size, query latency) and a build-time size report.

risk_register.description: Malformed YAML front matter in Markdown files causes the build process to fail (file-level or site-level).
XSS/content injection risk if note content (including raw HTML) is rendered into pages without proper sanitization/escaping, allowing malicious content to execute in the browser.

mitigation.text: Default to disallowing raw HTML in Markdown or sanitize it; ensure escaping of all user-controlled strings in templates; add security tests with known payloads; document trust model (personal notes vs shared).

risk_register.description: Sensitive/private information contained within notes is inadvertently published to a public host because access control is a non-goal and the user may not fully appreciate the exposure risk.

Backlink generation is incomplete or incorrect due to edge cases (anchors, aliases, transclusion-like links, duplicate titles) and/or circular link relationships causing faulty graph handling (e.g., infinite loop/stack overflow).

mitigation.text: Define canonical note identifiers (path-based) and maintain an explicit link graph; record link types and targets during parse; add graph consistency checks and backlink golden tests.

risk_register.description: File name, slug, or note title collisions map multiple notes to the same output path, causing overwrites and incorrect link/backlink resolution (e.g., multiple index.md files or duplicate titles).

mitigation.text: Define canonical note identifiers (path-based) and maintain an explicit link graph; record link types and targets during parse; add graph consistency checks and backlink golden tests.

risk_register.description: Build pipeline fails or produces incorrect output due to non-UTF8 files, unusual filenames, OS-specific path handling, and/or limited cross-platform support (Windows/macOS/Linux).

mitigation.text: Normalize and validate paths; define supported encodings; add cross-platform tests (Windows/Mac/Linux path separators); implement clear error messages and a file-skip option with reporting.

risk_register.description: Broken internal links are handled inconsistently (e.g., silent failures or crashes), leading to hidden navigation defects and reduced trust.

mitigation.text: Implement build-time link validation; provide strict/warn modes; generate a 'broken links' report artifact and optionally fail the build in CI.

risk_register.description: Broken relative paths/base URLs and/or absolute link generation break assets and navigation on common hosting targets (local file browsing vs subdirectory hosting such as GitHub Pages).

mitigation.text: Support configurable basePath/baseUrl (Q5); generate consistent absolute/relative URLs; add a deploy-target test matrix and a link checker against the built output directory.

risk_register.description: If incremental/watch mode is implemented, it produces stale pages or inconsistent search index compared to clean builds due to missed dependencies (e.g., templates/shared assets).

mitigation.text: Treat incremental build as an optional feature; add invariants to ensure incremental output matches clean build output; provide a 'clean' command and detect partial-state corruption.

risk_register.description: Generated site accessibility is poor (contrast, semantics/landmarks/ARIA, keyboard navigation), reducing usability for users with disabilities.

mitigation.text: Adopt an accessible base theme; run automated checks (e.g., semantic headings, alt text handling); document accessibility assumptions for user-supplied content.

risk_register.description: Generated site is not mobile-responsive or has poor usability on small screens, limiting utility for mobile readers.
Navigation/information architecture mismatches user expectations (missing pages, confusing tag index, poor discoverability).

mitigation.text: Resolve IA requirements (Q4); provide a minimal default nav (Home, All notes, Tags) plus configurable menus; include a generated sitemap page and consistent breadcrumbs.

risk_register.description: Search relevance quality is poor (stemming, ranking, stopwords), failing success expectations despite a functioning index.

mitigation.text: Define relevance acceptance tests (queries and expected top results); allow configuration of tokenization/stopwords; include title boosting and tag boosting where applicable.

risk_register.description: Template/theme customization introduces unsafe injections or code execution (e.g., user-provided templates/scripts) that compromise site integrity.

mitigation.text: Limit customization to safe configuration (CSS variables, allowed template slots); if templating is supported, sandbox and lint templates; document security boundaries and disable arbitrary JS by default.

risk_register.description: Non-deterministic builds (ordering differences, timestamps, locale/timezone differences) cause noisy diffs and unreliable deployment pipelines.

mitigation.text: Enforce deterministic ordering (sorted paths/tags); avoid embedding timestamps by default; control locale/timezone; add a 'deterministic build' CI check comparing repeated builds.

risk_register.description: Dependency supply-chain issues (vulnerable Markdown/render/search libraries) introduce security and maintenance risk.

mitigation.text: Pin dependencies; run vulnerability scanning in CI; maintain an upgrade cadence; prefer well-maintained libraries with security track records.

risk_register.description: Insufficient error messages/logging during build leads to long debugging cycles and poor user experience.

mitigation.text: Standardize structured logs and human-readable summaries; include file/line context where possible; provide a final build report with counts (notes, tags, links, warnings).

risk_register.description: CLI has complex installation steps or confusing UX, creating a barrier to entry for less technical users (relates to Q10).

restrictions.notes: Allow canonical audit-spine artifacts (run_manifest, event_log, stage_handoff).

hitl_triggers: Any request to access private repositories, personal notes, or credentials
Any ambiguity in requirements that changes scope beyond capsule goals/non-goals
Unconfirmed blocker questions (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q10) would materially change architecture or success metrics
Any decision affecting security boundaries (raw HTML, template execution, third-party JS/search libraries)
Proposed features conflict with non-goals (e.g., auth, server runtime, AI generation)
Proposed approach requires unsupported Markdown/linking/tag conventions without confirmation
Validation finds blockers that affect architecture (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q10)
Security risk identified that requires a trust-model decision (e.g., raw HTML handling)
Validation stage detects a high number of broken links or accessibility violations above a defined threshold.
Build time or memory usage exceeds performance targets for the specified note scale.

restrictions.value: all key claims must reference capsule fields or confirmed answers

hitl_triggers: Any acceptance of high/critical risks without mitigations
Any policy decision impacting user security (sanitization, template execution)
Tradeoff requires product decision (feature cuts, performance budgets, compatibility choices)
Any build process failure (e.g., crash, non-zero exit code).
Request to change scope or revise locked decisions

when_to_interrupt: Unconfirmed blocker questions (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q10) would materially change architecture or success metrics
Any decision affecting security boundaries (raw HTML, template execution, third-party JS/search libraries)
Any proposal that violates hard constraints (static-only output) or non-goals (server runtime, auth, AI content generation)
Any need to accept a high/critical risk without a mitigation plan
Any build process failure (e.g., crash, non-zero exit code).
Validation stage detects a high number of broken links or accessibility violations above a defined threshold.
Build time or memory usage exceeds performance targets for the specified note scale.

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be implemented for the MVP static-site generator?
decision_log.choice: Implement O1 (custom monolithic CLI pipeline) as the initial architecture.
decision_log.rationale: O1 meets the static-only constraint and all MUST requirements with minimal up-front complexity and fastest path to a working end-to-end build. Given open questions around conventions (Q1/Q2), a single cohesive pipeline is easier to iterate on than a plugin API or multi-stage caching system.
alternatives_considered: O2 (plugin-based core)
O3 (extend an existing SSG)
O4 (multi-stage pipeline with intermediate artifacts)
what_would_change_this_decision: If strong requirements emerge for third-party extensibility or multiple interchangeable Markdown/search backends (favor O2).
If watch mode/incremental builds become a primary requirement early (favor O4 or O3).
If the user already standardizes on an SSG ecosystem and wants to adopt its conventions/tooling (favor O3).

decision_log.question: What is the canonical note identifier used for output paths and link resolution?
decision_log.choice: Use a path-based canonical identifier derived from the note’s relative source path (with a deterministic slug/output-path mapping) and treat collisions as a build-time error or explicit disambiguation requirement.
decision_log.rationale: Path-based IDs are deterministic and avoid ambiguity from duplicate titles. This supports robust internal link resolution and stable URLs, and reduces overwrite risk (K10).
alternatives_considered: Title-based slugs as the primary identifier
Content-hash-based identifiers
User-supplied explicit IDs in front matter
what_would_change_this_decision: If the note ecosystem relies primarily on title-based linking (e.g., wiki-links) and titles are guaranteed unique by convention.
If the user demands stable URLs independent of file paths (e.g., to preserve external links).

decision_log.question: What link syntaxes are required for MVP internal links and how should additional syntaxes be handled?
decision_log.choice: MVP MUST support standard Markdown relative links to other Markdown notes (R9). Additional syntaxes (e.g., wiki-links) are treated as configurable extensions (R15) and should not be enabled by default until conventions are confirmed (Q1).
decision_log.rationale: R9 requires standard relative Markdown link resolution end-to-end; expanding beyond that without Q1 confirmation increases ambiguity and broken-link risk (K2).
alternatives_considered: Support wiki-links by default
Attempt to auto-detect link conventions without configuration
Support multiple link syntaxes concurrently without precedence rules
what_would_change_this_decision: Confirmed user requirement that wiki-links (or Obsidian-style variants) are the primary convention and must work for MVP.
Availability of a clear precedence and parsing spec from the user for mixed conventions.

decision_log.question: How are tags extracted and normalized across the site?
decision_log.choice: Implement a configurable tag extraction mode (at least one convention for MVP per R11) plus a single normalization pipeline applied everywhere (R16).
decision_log.rationale: Tag conventions are a known blocker (Q2) and a high risk (K3). Making extraction explicit and normalization consistent prevents duplicated/fragmented tag pages and supports predictable navigation.
alternatives_considered: Hard-code one convention without configuration
Treat tags as opaque strings with no normalization
Allow per-page ad hoc normalization behaviors
what_would_change_this_decision: If the user confirms a single unambiguous tag convention with strict rules and no need for configuration.
If the user requires preserving original tag casing/format exactly as authored, with normalization only for URLs.

decision_log.question: What is the default behavior for unresolved internal links?
decision_log.choice: Default to build-time warnings (not failure), include source context in messages, and render unresolved links as clearly non-navigable output; optionally provide a stricter mode later (R18).
decision_log.rationale: This matches the SHOULD requirement for broken-link handling (R18) and mitigates K12 without disrupting builds for minor issues. It also supports iterative cleanup while conventions are refined.
alternatives_considered: Fail the build on any unresolved link by default
Silently ignore unresolved links
Render unresolved links as normal links (leading to 404s)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the user intends to use this in CI/CD where broken links must block deployment by default.
If the note collection is expected to be fully consistent and strictness is preferred.

decision_log.question: What is the default security posture for rendering Markdown that may contain raw HTML?
decision_log.choice: Default to disallowing or sanitizing raw HTML in Markdown output and ensure template escaping for all user-controlled strings; document the trust model (related to K7).
decision_log.rationale: Notes may contain content that becomes executable in a browser if rendered unsafely. A safe default reduces XSS risk while still allowing a controlled opt-in if needed, which aligns with the risk register (K7).
alternatives_considered: Allow raw HTML passthrough by default
Strip all HTML aggressively without configurability
Rely on users to avoid unsafe content without sanitization
what_would_change_this_decision: If the user explicitly requires raw HTML support for trusted private notes and accepts the risk.
If the chosen Markdown renderer cannot safely sanitize and the project scope needs a different renderer or a strict HTML-escaping mode.

decision_log.question: What search indexing approach should be used to satisfy fully static, client-side search?
decision_log.choice: Generate a build-time search index artifact (e.g., JSON-based corpus/index data) and ship it with the site; implement browser-side search that queries this artifact without server requests (R7, R8), with basic reporting for index size/performance (R22 guidance).
decision_log.rationale: This directly satisfies the static constraint and MUST requirements for client-side search and build-time index generation. It also provides an anchor for later optimizations (chunking/lazy loading) if K5 becomes acute.
alternatives_considered: Server-side search
Rely on third-party hosted search services
No prebuilt index; fetch per-page content at query time
what_would_change_this_decision: If confirmed scale (Q3) makes a single shipped index impractically large, requiring chunking or a different representation.
If the user later accepts a non-static runtime (conflicts with constraints/non-goals).

decision_log.question: How should the generator handle deployments under subdirectories (base paths)?
decision_log.choice: Provide a base URL/path-prefix configuration and generate all internal URLs (note links, tag links, assets, search index fetch path) through a single URL-building helper to ensure consistency (R19).
decision_log.rationale: Subdirectory hosting is common and a frequent source of broken navigation/assets (K13). Centralizing URL generation reduces errors and simplifies testing across deployment targets.
alternatives_considered: Hard-code root-relative URLs
Only support relative URLs everywhere with no configuration
Defer base path support entirely
what_would_change_this_decision: If the user confirms a single deployment target that is always root-hosted and does not require base paths.
If the user requires local file browsing (file://) as a primary target, which may require stricter relative-path behavior.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Thin-slice milestone alignment to MUST requirements and acceptance tests
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Milestone 1 is scoped to lock in the end-to-end CLI build, static output, CommonMark rendering, and error handling (R1–R6) and immediately validates them via AT1–AT6. Milestones 2–4 add the remaining core MUST feature sets (tags, links/backlinks, search) and explicitly gate each via their mapped acceptance tests (AT7–AT13). Milestone 5 focuses on cross-browser QA (AT14) and key SHOULD items that materially affect real-world deployability and usability (R18–R21, R19).

synthesis_warnings.summary: Blocker convention questions remain unresolved (Q1 internal link syntax/precedence, Q2 tag conventions/normalization, Q4 information architecture, Q10 CLI vs other integration). These materially affect implementation details and test fixtures for links/tags/navigation and should be confirmed before or during Milestone 1–2 to avoid rework.

Security boundary decision is required for raw HTML handling and sanitization behavior because it affects XSS exposure (K7) and may trigger HITL policy review. This candidate assumes safe-by-default (sanitize/disallow raw HTML) but needs explicit approval if the user expects raw HTML passthrough.

Scale/performance expectations are not fully confirmed (Q3). Search-index representation and client-side performance (R22, K5) may need adjustment (e.g., chunking/lazy loading) if the dataset is significantly larger or heavier than anticipated.

glossary.definition: A website consisting of pre-generated files (e.g., HTML/CSS/JS) served without server-side rendering or a runtime database.
A lightweight markup language using plain text formatting syntax that converts to HTML.
A label associated with a note, used to group and browse notes by topic.
A reverse reference showing which other notes link to the current note.
Search that matches terms in the content of notes (not only titles/metadata), typically via a prebuilt index for static sites.
